$comment: Pocket Casts app screens, rendered from :modules:features:settings. This is the companion to the `pocketcasts` catalog and answers a different question. That one renders :modules:services:compose, which is a component library: its `Screens` section is two screen-shaped compositions assembled in `src/debug` out of the module's own app bar, sections and rows, because the app's actual screens live in feature modules that the component library cannot see. This spec renders a feature module directly, so every entry below is a screen the app really ships — the same composable, called with a hand-built state object instead of a view model. Settings is the feature module that goes first because its screens are self-contained: no player, no playback service, no infinite lists of network-loaded artwork. Getting here needed the screens to be functions of their inputs, which most of them already were; `HeadphoneControlsSettingsPage` and `StatusPageView` were hoisted for this, the former out of a Fragment whose rows reached for `childFragmentManager`. Two settings screens are deliberately absent: `HelpPage` is a WebView, so rendering it renders whatever support.pocketcasts.com served that morning, and `NotificationsTestingPage` is an internal debugging tool rather than product surface. Determinism is load-bearing, since the delivery branch is a force-pushed snapshot and the PNGs are diffed: the fixtures use pinned instants rather than `Date()`, artwork is switched off, and `ServiceStatus.Running` is avoided because its spinner has no settled frame. Unlike `pocketcasts` this catalog has no @PreviewParameter fan-out, so it renders strict — see the allow-incomplete note in design-artifacts.yml.
title: Pocket Casts Screens
library: Compose Material 2 + Pocket Casts theme roles

components.caption: Headphone controls: a summary paragraph over two action rows and a conditional toggle. The densest use of `SettingRow` in the app — icon, primary and secondary text, and a trailing switch all in one list.

variants.caption: With neither button bound to Add bookmark the confirmation sound row is not composed at all, so the screen is two rows shorter.
Tablet width — rows keep their fixed horizontal padding, so the extra width lands entirely between the label and the switch.

components.caption: The connection status report after a run. The one failed row is the interesting one: it swaps the service summary for help text and paints the failure message in `support05`, which is the role with the least contrast to work with in dark.

variants.caption: Before anything has been checked — a description and a single primary button on an otherwise empty screen.

components.caption: Up Next history: an explanatory paragraph over dated rows. Plain `TextH40` list rows with no leading icon or trailing control, which is the sparsest list style in the app.
One saved queue, with the formatted date promoted into the app bar title and a Restore text action beside it. Episode rows carry artwork, a three-line text block and a divider.
The log viewer: monospaced lines under an app bar that carries copy and share actions. The one screen here whose content is deliberately not styled by the design system.

variants.caption: With nothing to share the app bar's share action drops out — the only difference from the loaded state, and easy to regress unnoticed.

components.caption: The What's New sheet over a scrim: illustration header, headline, body and a full-width confirm button. The only modal in this catalog, and the only screen that dims what is behind it.

variants.caption: Shown to a user without the entitlement — the confirm button becomes the trial upsell, changing both the call to action and the sheet's height.

components.caption: The generic error state: a single centred line of `TextH50` under the screen's own app bar. Worth a sticker of its own because it is the shared shape every list screen in this module falls back to.
